slots.brief: The Last Fence — Kettlebrook's palisade gate creaks in the wind that rolls off the ruin country beyond. A rope-and-bell warning line marks where the town ends and the
The Council's Ledger — Elder Marlow Dunn keeps a grim tally of every party lost on the ruin road, chalked names never crossed out. He watches you with tired hope.
Senna Vey's Cottage — The widow's hands shake as she unrolls her late husband's map, its margins scrawled with warnings in a hand growing wilder toward the ruin's heart.
The Broker's Back Room — A one-eyed broker named Tull deals in salvage from the ruin road for those bold or foolish enough to buy secrets nobody else survived to sell.
The Dead Road — Beyond the fence the road turns to cracked stone and ash. Old wagon wheels lie half-buried, pointing every direction but forward.
The Silent Camp — Tents stand half-collapsed, cookfires long cold. Nothing here died violently — everything simply stopped, mid-motion.
The Cracked Bridge — A stone bridge spans a chasm of shifting ash-fog, its center span shattered and groaning under its own weight.
Ambush in the Ravine — Shapes drop from the rocks above — road bandits who've made a grim living picking through the belongings of those who never came back.
The Whispering Vault — A sealed door hums with warded glyphs that whisper half-words as you approach, as if trying to remember a language.
The Ghoul Warren — Beneath the vault, tunnels reek of old blood. Pale shapes uncoil from the dark, hungry for anything that still breathes.
The Hollow Choir — A cavern opens ahead, filled with a low, layered singing — the voices of everyone who never returned, bound together in the dark.
The Warden of the Choir — At the choir's heart stands a crowned, withered thing wreathed in cold light — the road's true warden, and the reason nobody comes back.
What the Road Demands — The warden is broken, and the choir's voices hang suspended, waiting on your next act to decide what the ruin road becomes.
